title: Kelly-sized tier recommender: spend proportional to edge and remaining budget
idea: Replace the flat work-shape lookup with a bankroll-management recommender modeled on the Kelly criterion, which sizes a bet by expected edge times bankroll. Score each unit on two axes the flat table ignores: payoff-at-stake (blast radius / irreversibility / whether it feeds a gated decision) and remaining run budget (bankroll). A unit that is high-stakes and early in the budget earns a Fable/xhigh recommendation with an explicit 'edge' justification; a low-stakes unit late in a depleted budget gets pushed down the ladder even if its work-shape would default high. The recommendation stays a deterministic, Claude-side heuristic that the operator confirms, never an external-engine gate. This produces the 'worth it, because' justification as a computed edge score rather than a category label, and it naturally starves the 'xhigh on everything' pattern once the bankroll runs thin.

The recommender is deterministic and advisory (operator confirms), so it respects {#external-engines-never-gatekeepers} (no engine adjudicates a gated decision) and stays within {#tier-vocab-ordering} by only moving along the ordered ladder.
